candidates.exact_span: The permittee must use sufficiently sensitive EPA-approved analytical methods (SSM) (under 40 CFR part 136 or required under 40 CFR chapter I, subchapters N or O) when quantifying the presence of pollutants in a discharge for analyses of pollutants or pollutant parameters under the permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether reported measurements were produced with SSM-compliant methods affects whether numeric results can be validly compared to discharge limits (A) and whether non-detect or low-value results reflect adequate analytical sensitivity versus missing or non-comparable evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: In case the approved methods are not sufficiently sensitive to the limits, the most SSM with the lowest method detection limit (MDL) must be used as defined under 40 CFR 122.44(i)(1)(iv)(A).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of when standard methods are 'not sufficiently sensitive to the limits' and which lowest-MDL SSM must be used can change which reported values are treated as quantified versus below-detection, altering exceedance determinations (A) and the evidentiary status of borderline or non-detect results (C).

candidates.exact_span: If no analytical laboratory is able to perform a test satisfying the SSM in the region, the most SSM with the lowest MDL must be used after adequate demonstrations by the permittee and EPA approval.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether this regional-unavailability exception and its demonstration/approval prerequisites are met can change which analytical method applies, whether numeric limit comparisons are possible (A), whether alternate monitoring/analytical obligations were in effect (B), and whether missing or qualified results should be treated as documented no-data, approved deviation, or unresolved (C).

candidates.exact_span: The Tijeras Arroyo (Canyon), a tributary to Rio Grande, is listed as being impaired for benthic-macroinvertebrate bioassessment and nutrient/eutrophication biological indicators and the probable cause include channelization, drought-related impacts, on site treatment systems, rangeland grazing, wastes from pets and unknown sources.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The identified impairment categories (bioassessment and nutrient/eutrophication biological indicators) could imply biological or related monitoring expectations; interpreting this listing affects which monitoring requirements are considered potentially applicable for the receiving water context (B).

candidates.exact_span: EPA does not consider that the discharger is a probable contributor to the impairment because of the nature of operation and the frequency of discharges.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The cited 'frequency of discharges' and operational characterization bear on whether discharge-conditioned monitoring was required during periods with no or infrequent discharge, affecting monitoring-obligation applicability (B) and how no-discharge or low-activity periods are classified in missing-evidence analysis (C).

candidates.exact_span: No additional pollutants are established to address the stream impairment.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This states that no extra pollutant-specific numeric limits were added for the 303(d) impairment; interpreting it affects which enforceable discharge limits are in scope for compliance comparison (A).

candidates.exact_span: A reopener language in the permit allows additional permit conditions if warranted by future changes and/or new TMDLs.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether reopener-triggering changes or new TMDLs occurred during Federal FY2025 could alter which limits and monitoring conditions were operative in that period versus left prospective or unresolved (A, B).

candidates.exact_span: The NMAC, Section 20.6.4.8 "Antidegradation Policy and Implementation Plan" sets forth the requirements to protect designated uses through implementation of the State water quality standards.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Cross-referencing this antidegradation implementation provision may import state water quality standards or antidegradation-derived constraints into the permit framework, potentially affecting which numeric limits and associated monitoring are considered applicable (A, B).
